scenes.heading: Similar triangles
scenes.say: Two triangles can have exactly the same shape but different sizes. In this video you will learn the four tests for similar triangles and use the scale factor to find missing sides.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A thumbnail is the same photo, shrunk evenly
scenes.science: Similar triangles: equal angles, every side scaled by the same k
scenes.breaks: Apps can crop or squash a thumbnail; a similar triangle uses one scale factor for every side.
scenes.say: The thumbnail of a photo on your phone is the same picture, just smaller. Every angle is the same and every length shrinks by the same amount. Similar triangles are a triangle and its thumbnail. But an app might squash a thumbnail, while a similar triangle always uses one scale factor for every side.

scenes.heading: The four similarity tests
points: AAA: two pairs of equal angles is enough
SSS: three side ratios all equal
SAS: two ratios equal + included angle
RHS: right angle, hypotenuse and side ratio
scenes.say: Here are the four tests. A A A: two pairs of equal angles is enough, because the third must match. S S S: all three side ratios are equal. S A S: two ratios are equal and the angle between those sides is equal. R H S: right angles, with the hypotenuses and one other pair of sides in the same ratio.

scenes.heading: A line parallel to one side
scenes.say: First the big triangle, then the line D E parallel to the base. The small triangle at the top is similar to the whole triangle. A D is four, but it matches the whole side A B, which is ten, not just D B. So the scale factor is two point five, and B C is five times two point five: twelve point five centimetres.
scenes.caption: The small triangle at the top is similar to the whole triangle. AD = 4 matches the whole side AB = 10, not just DB. So k = 2.5, and BC = 5 × 2.5 = 12.5 cm.

scenes.heading: The hourglass
scenes.say: Now an hourglass. A B is parallel to D E and the lines cross at C. The angles at C are vertically opposite, and the parallel lines give alternate angles, so the two triangles are similar. C E divided by A C is nine over six, one point five, so D E is eight times one point five: twelve centimetres.
scenes.caption: AB ∥ DE and the lines cross at C. Vertically opposite angles at C and alternate angles make the triangles similar. CE ÷ AC = 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5, so DE = 8 × 1.5 = 12 cm.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Sides 6, 8, 10 and 9, 12, 15. Similar?
scenes.say: Is a triangle with sides six, eight and ten similar to one with sides nine, twelve and fifteen? Match smallest with smallest. Nine over six, twelve over eight and fifteen over ten all give one point five, so yes, they are similar by S S S.

points: Similar: equal angles, sides in one ratio
scenes.say: Quick recap. Similar triangles have equal angles and all sides in the same ratio. The tests are A A A, S S S, S A S and R H S. A parallel line or an hourglass gives similar triangles. Match the whole side, and find k as large over small. Now try the practice questions!
